title: Penalty for illegally manufacturing or bottling liquor
description: Whoever in contravention of the provisions of this Act or of any rules, regulations or orders made thereunder, manufactures or bottles any liquor shall, on conviction, be punished for the first offence with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and with fine which may extend to five lakh rupees, and for any subsequent offence with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years and with fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees. The Bombay Prohibition Act, 1949 (Maharashtra) imposes strict penalties on illicit manufacture of liquor within the State.
chapter: Bombay Prohibition Act, 1949 - Offences and Penalties

title: Penalty for possession of illicit liquor or intoxicating drug
description: Whoever in contravention of the provisions of this Act or of any rules, regulations or orders made thereunder, possesses any liquor or any intoxicating drug shall, on conviction, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees. The burden of proving lawful possession lies on the accused.
chapter: Bombay Prohibition Act, 1949 - Offences and Penalties

title: Penalty for consuming liquor or using intoxicating drug
description: Whoever in contravention of the provisions of this Act or any rules, regulations or orders made thereunder, consumes or uses any liquor or any intoxicating drug shall, on conviction, be punished for the first offence with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both, and for any subsequent offence with imprisonment which may extend to three years and fine which may extend to twenty-five thousand rupees.
chapter: Bombay Prohibition Act, 1949 - Offences and Penalties

title: Penalty for causing death by consumption of illicit liquor
description: Whoever manufactures, sells or distributes any denatured spirituous preparation, or illicit liquor, the consumption of which causes death of any person, shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to fine which shall not be less than two lakh rupees. This stringent provision was added by Maharashtra Amendment to address hooch tragedies.
chapter: Bombay Prohibition Act, 1949 - Offences and Penalties (Maharashtra Amendment)

title: Penalty for selling or buying liquor
description: Whoever sells or buys, or offers or accepts for sale any liquor or any intoxicating drug in contravention of the provisions of this Act, shall on conviction be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees.
chapter: Bombay Prohibition Act, 1949 - Offences and Penalties

title: Penalty for being found drunk
description: Whoever is found in a state of intoxication in any public place or in any place to which the public have or are permitted to have access, shall, on conviction, be punished for the first offence with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months and for any subsequent offence with imprisonment which may extend to one year.
chapter: Bombay Prohibition Act, 1949 - Offences and Penalties

title: Penalty for keeping a common gaming house
description: Any person who opens, keeps, or uses any house, room, or place as a common gaming house, and any person who being the owner or occupier or having the use of any house, room, or place, knowingly or wilfully permits the same to be opened, kept, or used as a common gaming house by any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees, or with both. Under the Bombay Prevention of Gambling Act, 1887, this provision targets organized gambling operations.
chapter: Bombay Prevention of Gambling Act, 1887 - Offences

title: Penalty for gaming in common gaming house
description: Whoever is found in any common gaming house during any gaming or playing therein, shall be liable to a fine not exceeding one hundred rupees or to imprisonment for any term not exceeding one month. Under Bombay Prevention of Gambling Act, 1887, mere presence in a gaming house during gaming creates a presumption of guilt.
chapter: Bombay Prevention of Gambling Act, 1887 - Offences

title: Online gaming and betting
description: Any person who organizes, manages, or promotes online gaming or betting in contravention of this Act shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and with fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees. This provision was added by the Maharashtra Amendment to the Bombay Prevention of Gambling Act to address digital gambling platforms. Playing games of skill for stakes is excluded from this provision.
chapter: Bombay Prevention of Gambling Act, 1887 - Maharashtra Amendment

title: Power to regulate assemblies and processions and use of music
description: The District Magistrate or the Commissioner of Police may, whenever and for so long as he considers necessary for the preservation of public peace or public safety or for the maintenance of public order, by general or special order, make rules or give directions to regulate the conduct of assemblies and processions on or along the streets and the route by which and the times at which such processions may pass.
chapter: Bombay Police Act, 1951 - Preventive Action of Police

title: Order prohibiting assemblies in certain areas
description: The Commissioner of Police or the District Magistrate may, whenever he considers it necessary so to do for the preservation of public peace or public safety or for the maintenance of public order, by order in writing, prohibit in any area or place within the local limits of his jurisdiction any assembly of five or more persons or any procession. This provision is frequently invoked alongside Section 144 CrPC for crowd control in Mumbai and Maharashtra.
chapter: Bombay Police Act, 1951 - Preventive Action of Police

title: Punishment for contravention of prohibitory orders
description: Whoever contravenes any prohibitory order made under Section 37 shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both. Under the Bombay Police Act, 1951, breach of prohibitory orders is a cognizable offence.
chapter: Bombay Police Act, 1951 - Penalties and Procedure

title: Prohibition of nuisance by noise or music
description: No person shall beat any drum, tom-tom, or other instrument, or blow any horn, trumpet or other instrument, or make or cause any noise, sound, or music likely to cause annoyance to the inhabitants of any street between the hours of 10 PM and 6 AM without the written permission of the Commissioner of Police or the District Superintendent of Police.
chapter: Bombay Police Act, 1951 - Regulation of Public Conduct

title: Penalty for disobedience of police officer's order
description: Whoever, without lawful excuse, disobeys any direction lawfully given by a police officer, shall on conviction be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. This is a widely invoked provision under the Bombay Police Act, 1951.
chapter: Bombay Police Act, 1951 - Penalties and Procedure

title: Definition of continuing unlawful activity
description: Continuing unlawful activity means an activity prohibited by law for the time being in force, which is a cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment of three years or more, undertaken either singly or jointly, as a member of an organised crime syndicate or on behalf of such syndicate in respect of which more than one charge-sheet has been filed before a competent Court within the preceding period of ten years, and that Court has taken cognizance of such offence.
chapter: MCOCA, 1999 - Definitions

title: Definition of organised crime
description: Organised crime means any continuing unlawful activity by an individual, singly or jointly, either as a member of an organised crime syndicate or on behalf of such syndicate, by use of violence or threat of violence or intimidation or coercion, or other unlawful means, with the objective of gaining pecuniary benefits, or gaining undue economic or other advantage for himself or any other person, or promoting insurgency.
chapter: MCOCA, 1999 - Definitions

title: Definition of organised crime syndicate
description: Organised crime syndicate means a group of two or more persons who, acting either singly or collectively, as a syndicate or gang, indulge in activities of organised crime. The Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA), 1999, provides a broad definition to target criminal syndicates operating in Maharashtra.
chapter: MCOCA, 1999 - Definitions

title: Punishment for organised crime
description: Whoever commits an offence of organised crime shall, (i) if such offence has resulted in the death of any person, be punishable with death or imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to a fine of a minimum of one lakh rupees; (ii) in any other case, be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to a fine of a minimum of five lakh rupees.
chapter: MCOCA, 1999 - Offences and Penalties

title: Punishment for attempting or conspiring to commit organised crime
description: Whoever conspires or attempts to commit or advocates, abets or knowingly facilitates the commission of an offence of organised crime or any act preparatory to organised crime, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to a fine of minimum one lakh rupees.
chapter: MCOCA, 1999 - Offences and Penalties

title: Punishment for harbouring or concealing a member of organised crime syndicate
description: Whoever harbours or conceals or attempts to harbour or conceal any member of an organised crime syndicate shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to a fine of minimum one lakh rupees.
chapter: MCOCA, 1999 - Offences and Penalties

title: Punishment for possession of property derived from organised crime
description: Any person who is a member of an organised crime syndicate and who is, or at any time has been, in possession of movable or immovable property which he cannot satisfactorily account for, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine of minimum one lakh rupees.
chapter: MCOCA, 1999 - Offences and Penalties

title: Punishment for possessing arms and explosives in certain areas
description: Whoever in any area declared to be a disturbed area possesses any arms or explosives or substances, whether biological or chemical, of such nature as may be notified, in contravention of any law for the time being in force, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to fine.
chapter: MCOCA, 1999 - Offences and Penalties

title: Modified application of certain provisions of CrPC
description: Where the offence is punishable with imprisonment for a term of three years or more but not more than seven years, the Special Court may, notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, release the accused person on bail if it thinks fit. However, no person accused of an offence punishable under this Act shall be released on bail unless the Public Prosecutor has been given an opportunity to oppose the application for bail. The limitation on bail under MCOCA is one of its most significant provisions.
chapter: MCOCA, 1999 - Special Courts and Procedure

title: Admissibility of confessions made to police officers
description: Notwithstanding anything in the Code of Criminal Procedure or in the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, a confession made by a person before a police officer not below the rank of Superintendent of Police, and recorded by such police officer either in writing or on any mechanical device, shall be admissible in the trial of such person for an offence under this Act. This is a significant departure from normal evidence rules where confessions to police are inadmissible.
chapter: MCOCA, 1999 - Evidence

title: Protection of witnesses
description: The Special Court may, on an application made by a witness in any proceeding before it or by the Public Prosecutor in relation to such witness or on its own motion, take such measures as it deems fit for keeping the identity and address of the witness secret. The identity protection provisions under MCOCA are among the strongest witness protection mechanisms in Indian law.
chapter: MCOCA, 1999 - Evidence and Witness Protection

title: Interception of wire, electronic or oral communication
description: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any police officer not below the rank of Superintendent of Police, supervising the investigation of an offence under this Act, may submit an application in writing to the competent authority for an order for the interception of wire, electronic or oral communication if there are reasonable grounds to believe that such interception may provide evidence of an offence under this Act.
chapter: MCOCA, 1999 - Interception

title: Maharashtra Amendment to Criminal Conspiracy (IPC Section 120B)
description: The State of Maharashtra has applied enhanced provisions for criminal conspiracy when the conspiracy relates to offences affecting public order or communal harmony within the State. Under the Bombay Amendment, conspiracy charges in conjunction with offences under the Bombay Police Act or Maharashtra state laws carry enhanced penalties beyond the Central IPC provisions.
chapter: Maharashtra Amendments to IPC - Conspiracy

title: Maharashtra Amendment to Promoting Enmity (IPC Section 153A)
description: Maharashtra has enhanced enforcement of Section 153A IPC through State-specific rules under the Bombay Police Act. Promoting enmity between groups in the context of communal tensions in Maharashtra, especially in Mumbai and other urban centres, is treated with enhanced police powers under the combined operation of the Bombay Police Act and the IPC provision.
chapter: Maharashtra Amendments to IPC - Communal Offences

title: Maharashtra Amendment to Outraging Religious Feelings (IPC Section 295A)
description: Under Maharashtra's enforcement framework, deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings are subject to enhanced investigation and prosecution procedures. The State has established special cells for communal offences that operate under the combined framework of Section 295A IPC and the Bombay Police Act.
chapter: Maharashtra Amendments to IPC - Religious Offences

title: Standard rent and permitted increases
description: Under the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999 (replacing the earlier Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947), standard rent means the rent at which the premises were let on the date of the commencement of this Act or the agreed rent, whichever is less. Landlords may apply for an increase of rent once in two years not exceeding four percent of the cost of the premises. This provision balances tenant protection with landlord rights in Maharashtra.
chapter: Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999 - Rent Control

title: Protection against eviction of tenants
description: A landlord shall not be entitled to recover possession of any premises so long as the tenant pays, or is ready and willing to pay, the amount of the standard rent and permitted increases, if any, and observes and performs the other conditions of the tenancy. The Maharashtra Rent Control Act provides strong anti-eviction protections derived from the original Bombay Rent Act, 1947.
chapter: Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999 - Eviction

title: Declaration of areas as Development Zones
description: Under the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966, the State Government may declare any area in the State as a development zone for the purposes of development or redevelopment of such area. This provision was used extensively for the development of Mumbai's infrastructure including the Coastal Regulation Zone enforcement, Slum Rehabilitation Schemes, and Transit-Oriented Development.
chapter: MRTP Act, 1966 - Development Control

title: Prohibition of accepting deposits fraudulently
description: No person shall accept deposits from depositors by making a fraudulent default. Under the Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors (in Financial Establishments) Act, 1999, any financial establishment that accepts deposits and commits fraud shall be liable for imprisonment which may extend to ten years and fine which shall not be less than the amount of deposits accepted.
chapter: MPID Act, 1999 - Prohibition and Penalties

title: Attachment of property of defaulting financial establishments
description: Where a financial establishment has made a fraudulent default in repayment of deposits, the Competent Authority may attach the properties, movable and immovable, belonging to such financial establishment or its promoters, directors, partners or managers. The MPID Act empowers special courts to order attachment before conviction, which is a departure from general criminal procedure.
chapter: MPID Act, 1999 - Attachment and Recovery
